question.text: Starting with the same initial conditions, an ideal gas expands from volume <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>V</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>V</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> in three different ways. The work done by the gas is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> if the process is purely isothermal, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>, if the process is purely adiabatic and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> if the process is purely isobaric. Then, choose the correct option
